Container.Name: aria2-direct
Container.Overview:
Download files directly to your server using aria2 and the bundled AriaNg web interface. Supports HTTP(S), FTP and SFTP, persistent queues, resumable downloads and browser-extension/API submission. BitTorrent and Metalink are unavailable.
Intended for a trusted LAN. Automatic RPC-secret setup is enabled: anyone who can load the web interface can recover the secret and control downloads. Leave the secret blank to generate one on first start.
Review the download path before applying. When replacing another aria2 image, use a fresh config directory; its old configuration may contain unsupported torrent settings. If you change the host-side RPC port, set AriaNg RPC Port to the same value.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Host port for AriaNg. Changing this host port does not require any environment-variable changes.

Config.Name: RPC Port
Config.Description: Host port used by your browser, extensions and API clients to reach aria2. If changed, update AriaNg RPC Port below as well.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Persistent configuration, RPC secret and download queue. Use a fresh directory when migrating from another image.

Config.Name: Downloads
Config.Description: Download destination, including unfinished files and their .aria2 resume metadata. Choose your actual download share; preserve this data between restarts.

Config.Name: RPC Secret
Config.Description: Optional secret without surrounding quotes. Leave blank to reuse the saved secret or generate one on first start. No line breaks or leading/trailing whitespace.

Config.Name: Auto-fill RPC Secret
Config.Description: Automatically supply the secret to AriaNg. Anyone who can load the UI can retrieve it. Set false to enter the secret manually instead.

Config.Name: AriaNg RPC Port
Config.Description: Host-side RPC port AriaNg connects to. Must match the RPC Port mapping above. The internal RPC port stays 6800.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Container timezone, for example Etc/UTC or Europe/Oslo.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: File-owner user ID. Unraid normally uses 99 for nobody. Existing download subdirectories must be writable by this user/group.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: File-owner group ID. Unraid normally uses 100 for users.

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: Permissions mask for newly created files. Use 002 if you want group-write permission on downloads.
